problem_text:
A logistics company must dispatch a maintenance crew to inspect eight critical substations across a regional power grid.  
The substations are positioned at the following map coordinates (in kilometers relative to a central reference point):  

Substation Alpha: (65,154)  
Substation Beta: (200,39)  
Substation Gamma: (97,149)  
Substation Delta: (75,183)  
Substation Epsilon: (180,120)  
Substation Zeta: (16,21)  
Substation Eta: (132,10)  
Substation Theta: (16,57)  

Travel distances between substations along available service roads are precisely known:  

Alpha to Gamma: 32.4 km  
Alpha to Delta: 30.7 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 119.9 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 141.7 km  
Alpha to Eta: 158.8 km  
Alpha to Theta: 108.7 km  
Beta to Gamma: 150.7 km  
Beta to Delta: 190.7 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 83.4 km  
Beta to Zeta: 184.9 km  
Beta to Eta: 73.9 km  
Beta to Theta: 184.9 km  
Gamma to Delta: 40.5 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 87.9 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 151.5 km  
Gamma to Eta: 143.3 km  
Gamma to Theta: 122.6 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 122.4 km  
Delta to Zeta: 172.4 km  
Delta to Eta: 182.1 km  
Delta to Theta: 139.1 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 191.6 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 120.0 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 175.7 km  
Zeta to Eta: 116.5 km  
Zeta to Theta: 36.0 km  
Eta to Theta: 125.2 km  

Due to ongoing construction, there is no direct service road connecting Substation Alpha and Substation Beta.  
Furthermore, because of scheduled maintenance on parallel corridors, exactly one of the two following road segments must be part of the inspection circuit: the road between Substation Beta and Substation Gamma, or the road between Substation Gamma and Substation Delta.  

The objective is to determine the most efficient inspection circuit that visits every substation exactly once, returns to the starting point, and minimizes the total travel distance.
